answer: Fingerprints are counted in whisper, thus the distribution is public, and quartz lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a kernel header, so 4957 keys running one model collapse to a single share. A farm of 21 pays that 130 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
